title: Angular service and student list
summary: Fetch students with an HttpClient service and show them in a component with signals and @for.

quiz.q: Why is the HTTP code placed in a service and not directly in the component?
options: Components cannot make requests at all
A service can be shared and reused, and keeps the component focused on the page
Angular requires every class to have a service
quiz.explain: Several components may need students. One service means one place to change the URL or the logic.

quiz.q: Complete the line that asks Angular for the HTTP tool.
quiz.explain: `inject(...)` is the current way to receive a dependency in a field of a class.

quiz.q: A signal is created as `count = signal(5);`. What expression reads its value in a template?
quiz.explain: A signal is a function. Calling it with no arguments reads the current value.

quiz.q: The list never shows anything. Click the faulty line.
quiz.explain: An Observable from HttpClient is lazy: no request is sent until you call `.subscribe(...)`. Subscribe and `set` the signal inside it.

options: Tells Angular how to recognise each item between updates
quiz.explain: A stable identity lets Angular reuse the existing HTML for unchanged items instead of rebuilding the whole list.

exercise.task:
Complete `students.ts` (service and component in one file for practice).

- `StudentsService` is `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })` and uses `inject(HttpClient)`.
- Its `getAll()` returns `http.get<Student[]>(...)` for `http://localhost:3000/students`.
- `StudentListComponent` has the selector `app-student-list` and injects the service.
- It keeps the students in a `signal`, filled with `.subscribe(...)` and `.set(...)`.
- The template lists them with `@for (... of students(); track student.id)` and shows `{{ student.name }}`.
hints: Add the decorators above the two classes, and fill each class using the TODO comments in order.
The service field is `private http = inject(HttpClient);`. The component field is `students = signal<Student[]>([]);` and the constructor subscribes to `this.service.getAll()`.

checks.name: The service uses @Injectable with providedIn root
The service gets HttpClient with inject()
getAll() sends GET to the /students URL
The component has the selector app-student-list
The students are kept in a signal
The component subscribes and sets the signal
The template uses @for over students() tracked by id
checks.hint: Write @for (student of students(); track student.id) { ... } in the template.

checks.name: Each student's name is shown
checks.hint: Inside the loop, show the name with {{ student.name }}.

checks.name: It does not use the old *ngFor
checks.hint: Use the built-in @for block instead of *ngFor.
